change.summary: Observed-run tree tracking no longer runs the blocking ps reader. Sampling uses a new async reader (execFile, same 100 ms ps timeout, same empty-table-on-failure contract) with an in-flight guard: a 25 ms tick that finds a sample in flight is skipped, so samples never overlap. quiesce clears the interval, awaits any in-flight sample (bounded by the remaining cleanup window, so an orphaned descendant seen only by that sample is still retained), then takes its final readings with the async reader and signals/polls exactly as before. kill() (one-shot) is unchanged and still enumerates synchronously before signalling.
change.notChanged: No deadline, limit, interval, ps timeout or test tolerance changed. runCoordinator.ts not touched.

finding.status: Starvation fixed; gate NOT green: lost-control-body still fails intermittently (8/10 in the isolated loop)
finding.decomposition: cutoff = 2000 - (revokedAt - nominalPollStart) + deadlineTimerLateness. Overruns are now 0.24-2.27 ms (before: up to ~20 ms). Last runs: headroom (revokedAt - nominal poll start) 1.6-1.9 ms; deadline timer lateness 0.6-0.9 ms. The headroom is only the control request's own latency, because startControlPoll anchors windowEnd at the nominal poll start + 2000 ms. A non-starved Node timer is still ~1-2 ms late (ms-granular libuv clock), so the race stays roughly even.
finding.inference: Before the fix the tick for the revoking poll was itself delayed by blocking ps calls, which widened the headroom by chance. Removing the blocking narrowed both sides, which is probably why the isolated fail rate rose from 2/5 to 8/10. This is an inference from the decomposition; it was not separately measured.
finding.remainingCause: Product-side, in src/server/runCoordinator.ts startControlPoll: the secret-bearing window has no scheduling margin for timer resolution, so meeting AC-13's 2 s bound depends on sub-millisecond timer accuracy.
finding.recommendation: @architect/lead decision (changes the AC-13 control-window timing, which is not tracker work): arm the secret-bearing deadline a fixed resolution margin early (for example, stop at windowEnd - N ms, with N >= the observed 2-3 ms timer lateness). This tightens the bound and does not loosen it. Unit tests in test/server/observedReplayAdmission.test.ts drive this window with an injected lateness clock and will need their expected values reviewed.
